hints.content:
We are asked whether the time it took to fully charge the battery can be represented as a function of the battery's capacity when the charging began. Therefore, in this case, **Initial capacity** is the **independent** (or **domain**) variable and **Time to charge** is the **dependent** (or **range**) variable.

Now we can view the table as if it describes a mapping from the domain of battery capacities to the range of durations (see below). A mapping like this represents a function if and only if *every* domain value is mapped to *exactly one* range value.

To put it another way, if we can find a domain value that is mapped to more than one range value, then the table cannot represent a function. Based on this principle, can this table represent a function?

|||||| |||
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
**Domain** | $65$ | $40$ | $30$ | $45$ | $65$ | $10$ | $30$ | $25$
**Range** | $20$ | $30$ | $34$ | $27$ | $18$ | $40$ | $32$ | $36$

By inspection of the table, we can see that the domain value $\blue{65}$ is mapped to both the range value $\pink{20}$ and the range value $\pink{18}$. In other words, *if we know that the battery's capacity when the charging began was $\textit{65}$ percentage points, we cannot be certain about the time it took to fully charge the battery.*

This isn't the only case where a domain value is mapped to more than one range value, but even a single case is enough to determine that the table cannot represent a function.

|||||| |||
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
**Domain** | $\blue{65}$ | $40$ | $30$ | $45$ | $\blue{65}$ | $10$ | $30$ | $25$
**Range** | $\pink{20}$ | $30$ | $34$ | $27$ | $\pink{18}$ | $40$ | $32$ | $36$

No!

The time it took to fully charge the battery *cannot* be represented as a function of the battery's capacity when the charging began.

question.content:
The table compares the capacity of Omojobi's phone's battery when he started charging it (in percentage points) and the time it took the battery to be fully charged (in minutes), for several different occasions.

**Can the time it takes to fully charge the battery be represented as a function of the battery's capacity when the charging begins?**

$40$ | $30$
$30$ | $34$
